articleTitle: Flexible Process Control for Scalable Electrolysis Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Large-scale water electrolysis systems are built from a multitude of stack units. These stack units have to be controlled during operation. The question arises how process control of the system can be designed in that way, that scalable, extendable but also optimal operation of the stack units becomes possible. To achieve this goal, existing process control strategies from literature are analyzed. The requirements resulting from the inherent numbering up of stack units are described and an approach for an adaptable optimized process control strategy considering the system properties is proposed. The proposed process control strategy is implemented in a modeled electrolysis system and evaluated regarding the stated criteria. The results could show, that the inherent modularization of electrolysis systems can be used in advantage for a scalable operation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of S1 and S2 Sounds Localization Methods in a Phonocardiogram
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The phonocardiogram (PCG) signal is an acoustic signal resulting from the mechanical functioning of the human heart. Although neglected today, its use with various technological advances brings a lot of information about the state of the heart. The aim of our work is to identify the most efficient method for the detection of B1 and B2 sounds in a PCG signal. Three methods were analyzed throughout our work. These are the Shannon Energy, the Hilbert Transform and the Continuous Wavelet Transform. Our analysis was based on 90 PCG recordings from normal subjects from the Pascal Classifying Heart Sound Challenge database. Our results showed that the Shannon energy exhibits the least detection error. Indeed, out of 1420 noises to be detected on the 90 recordings of PCG signals used, the implementation of the Shannon energy that we made presented 59 detection errors while the Hilbert transform and the continuous wavelet transform presented respectively 84 and 185 detection errors.

articleTitle: Equivariant Map and Agent Geometry for Autonomous Driving Motion Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In autonomous driving, deep learning enabled motion prediction is a popular topic. A critical gap in traditional motion prediction methodologies lies in ensuring equivariance under Euclidean geometric transformations and maintaining invariant interaction relationships. This research introduces a groundbreaking solution by employing EqMotion, a theoretically geometric equivariant and interaction invariant motion prediction model for particles and humans, plus integrating agent-equivariant high-definition (HD) map features for context aware motion prediction in autonomous driving. The use of EqMotion as backbone marks a significant departure from existing methods by rigorously ensuring motion equivariance and interaction invariance. Equivariance here implies that an output motion must be equally transformed under the same Euclidean transformation as an input motion, while interaction invariance preserves the manner in which agents interact despite transformations. These properties make the network robust to arbitrary Euclidean transformations and contribute to more accurate prediction. In addition, we introduce an equivariant method to process the HD map to enrich the spatial understanding of the network while preserving the overall network equivariance property. By applying these technologies, our model is able to achieve high prediction accuracy while maintain a lightweight design and efficient data utilization.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Converter Design to Interface Solar to Inductive Cooking in Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: To improve the quality of life in remote rural areas, electrification is of importance. Electrification using solar panels, for lighting and charging mobile phones, is already taking place. Especially air pollution during cooking on wood-powered stoves, can and should be replaced by cooking on solar power. Solar power is harvested per household and can be shared via a DC micro-grid. Electric cooking is the subject in this paper, and a converter is proposed to connect a low-cost commercially available induction cooker to a DC micro-grid containing multiple typical solar/battery installations. The DC micro-grid voltage cannot be directly used for the induction cooker, as it is higher than the required maximum of AC 250 volt RMS. A 1kW Buck converter is designed, capable of converting the DC micro-grid voltage of 300-400 volt, down to 230 volt DC, being the nominal voltage level for a commercially available induction cooker.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics on Used Car Prices Using Business Intelligence of Bayesian Networks for Sales Risk Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Used car prices are normally estimated at the time of initial purchase when the car is freshly purchased. Due to the shortage of cars from car manufacturers during the pandemic periods, secondhand car dealers have gained an undue advantage by withholding some information about cars advertised online. Researchers have tried to develop models to address this issue. There has not been enough research done in the area of uncertainty (partial observability) about used car prices. This research develops three transparent probabilistic models: a generalized model for all used cars, a specialized model for luxury cars, and a specialized model for non-luxury cars. It is intended to determine which models best predict used car prices. Publicly available car datasets were sourced, cleaned, and processed to build the models. Experimental evaluations reveal that the generalized model predicts prices with an accuracy of 80.19%, the specialized BN model for non-luxury cars predicts prices with an accuracy of 80.13% while the specialized BN model for luxury cars predicts prices with an accuracy of 83.5%. The results suggest that a specialized model performs better when predicting luxury used car prices. However, with non-luxury used cars, any of the two models predict prices satisfactorily. This research is aimed at helping used car buyers get a fair idea of expected selling prices, reducing risks using lower and upper bound prices. A new car buyer can also apply this model to estimate how much their car will be worth after a few years, which could aid in reaching sound business decisions.

articleTitle: Decentralised Digital Identity and Verifiable Credential Tracking and Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Digital identity has rapidly gained interest as organisations strive toward digital transformation. However, the lack of adequate digital identity management mechanisms has become a major concern. Consequently, decentralised digital identities are increasingly being used as a form of credentialing. This requires secure, reliable, scalable and privacy-preserving credential issuance and verification mechanisms to prove the legitimacy of the credential. On the other hand, most existing systems provide centralised solutions that primarily rely on third parties. Meanwhile, these systems do not allow end-users to own, control, and share their credentials with relevant parties. This paper proposes a secure and reliable de centralised digital identity, verifiable credential tracking, and management system. The proposed system guarantees the authenticity and integrity of the user credentials and allows users to selectively share a subset of their verifiable credentials with relevant stakeholders through the model known as self-sovereign identity (SSI). SSI facilitates end users to have sole ownership over the ability to control their accounts and personal data. To achieve the objectives of the study, the proposed system adopts the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), Decentralised Identifiers (DIDs), Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs). The system outperforms competitors in terms of both storage and speed and, thus, delivers exceptional efficiency and interoperability.

articleTitle: Equipment for Increasing the Phototrophic Microalgae Production at Lab Scale
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The human activities, especially the energy production from fossil fuels and the transport sector, produce huge amounts of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, which is a greenhouse gas [1]. In this context, developing and expanding phototrophic microalgae production is a suitable way to reduce the greenhouse effect by converting the anthropogenic CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> into organic mass and oxygen. It should be also mentioned that the organic mass, including algae, is a high added value product.

articleTitle: Residual Value of Used Car Analysis and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Car leasing is one of the most important business segments for automakers. The residual value plays a predominant role in determining the monthly installment in a lease agreement. Precision in forecasting a car's future residual value holds paramount importance for leasing companies. This study delves into the exploration of machine learning methodologies for the prediction of residual value. The study is based on real resale records of over 7,800 off-lease cars collected from one of the largest financial service companies in New Zealand. Additionally, macroeconomic variables such as GDP, CPI, interest rate, and used car index are included in the modeling process. We construct and assess the effectiveness of seven machine learning models. Our experimentation reveals that our CatBoost-based model attains a remarkable accuracy. It also halves the prediction error of the existing approach.

articleTitle: Exploring User Interactions in AR/VR Interfaces: A Simulation-Based Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies have gained significant attention in various domains. User interactions and error rates in VR/AR environments are crucial for improving system performance and user experience. In this study, a simulated dataset of 20,000 data points representing interactions of 1,000 users with four actions: “Select,” “Drag,” “Resize,” and “Rotate” is presented. Likelihood analysis is employed to explore error rates and their correlations with user-related factors such as action duration, fatigue, task success, preference, and learning rate. The findings deepen the understanding of error rates in VR/AR environments and provide insights into optimizing user experiences. The methodology of using simulated data and likelihood analysis can serve as a foundation for future studies investigating error modeling and prediction in real-world VR/AR applications.

articleTitle: Matrix Converter Gate Drive Control Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: One application of a matrix converter is in controlling the speed of an induction motor which make an AC-AC converter attractive. This application of the topology has some challenges. This paper presents the design of a matrix converter gate drive control circuit to address this challenge. Two known facts that pose this challenge in matrix converters are, firstly, over-voltages that occur whenever a switch is turned off across an inductive load and secondly, the occurrence of short-circuit currents whenever any lines connected in the process. In this paper, an is made to resolve the impact of the two constraints. The over-voltage constraint is solved by switching across an inductive load momentarily thereby providing a freewheeling path for current. The short-circuit constraint is resolved by implementing deadtime between successive switching pulses. This paper presents the design of the gate drive circuit to solve the short-circuit problem in such a way that a deadtime was realized through the delay circuit design whereas the overvoltage is achieved through switching across the load during the deadtime period.

articleTitle: Image Fusion Technique Using Singular Value Decomposition Based Undecimated Subband Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Image fusion is an important area of research. In remote sensing, the usage of the same sensor in different working modes, or different image sensors, can provide complementary information. Therefore, it is needed to fuse outputs from multiple sensors (or the same sensor in different working modes) to improve the performance of the remote images, which are very useful for many image processing tasks. Singular Value Decomposition Undecimated Subband Decomposition (SVD-USBD) of images with its Multi-Resolution schemes and based on it novel image fusion technique have been presented. The performance of this algorithm is compared with that of often used image fusion technique using Multi-Resolution form of Singular Value Decomposition (MR-SVD). It is observed that image fusion by SVD-USBD provides almost similar fusion quality and that is why it can be used in combinations with other methods to develop hybrid schemes for multi-focus image fusion or fusion of different types of images as infrared or termal imaging.

articleTitle: Using Artificial Intelligence for Padel Training
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Padel is a racket sport that has seen a surge in popularity in recent years. It is a mix of tennis and squash and is most played in doubles. It is played in what appears to be a smaller tennis court, however, its novelty is the fact that its court is contained within a combination of glass walls and metallic mesh. Machine learning and AI (artificial intelligence) have also gained great momentum in recent times. In a sporting application, it has been shown that the use of integrated machine learning training programs can improve player performance, either through improved form or better load management. Due to Padel's recent emergence, these technologies have not been investigated for this sport specifically. Therefore, in this paper, we will utilize computer vision, machine learning, and 3D visualization to create a prototype and proof of concept for such a system. The system is broken down into two main segments, the computer vision and machine learning aspect, and the 3D modeling and visualization aspect. The prototype system was tested using two player types to attempt to evaluate its effectiveness and highlight any weaknesses or room for improvement for a complete system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Cost FPGA Based Real-Time Simulator for a Three-Phase Grid Emulator Including Neutral
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents the design and the implementation of a low-cost FPGA-based real-time simulator for a grid emulation system including neutral. The real-time simulator for the proposed grid emulator is implemented in an open-loop version. No feedback mechanism or specific controllers are needed. That makes the design simple, low-cost, fast, and easy to implement while reducing the risk of system instability. The design process combines high-level Simulink models with HDL code generation and FPGA synthesis implementation in order to control the grid emulator. The control of the three-phase four-leg grid emulator is implemented using a PWM method based on a triangular carrier wave involving the concept of offset voltage to reach better PWM performances while reducing FPGA resource utilization. Experimental results carried out show the effectiveness of the proposed design that can track the reference with high precision, less than 1.6% of relative error compared to the reference, while achieving fast transient performance.

articleTitle: Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) in Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This article presents the results of the validation and design of a web application to find super-efficiency in productive companies in the city of Medellin in the country Colombia. In the sector, it is observed that there is a need to strengthen tools in operations research in companies where productive management processes are led. This type of management is carried out in an operational, non-technological manner. That is why an application called DEA 4.0 is being developed. This application addresses leadership and production process management by optimizing outcomes using mathematical models. These models enable a quicker and more precise comparison of measurement units, facilitating the optimization of processes to be evaluated. “Super Efficiency” models are part of the Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) field, which in turn is a subfield of Operations Research. The software product is validated within an artisanal productivity company by comparing the results of two models that exhibit better optimization responses. This enables the generation of conclusions for the decision process.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Electroluminescence Imaging for Solar PV Inspection Using a Modified Consumer Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As the adoption of renewable energy surges, the global proliferation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems intensifies. However, PV panels remain vulnerable to defects during transportation, installation, and harsh weather exposures, compromising their longevity and efficiency. Traditional visual and I-V curve tests, frequently employed for PV system maintenance, often fall short due to their restricted defective detection capacity, and extended inspection durations. While infrared (IR) and electroluminescence (EL) imaging methods excel in efficiency, their accompanying equipment is prohibitively expensive. Addressing this gap, the paper introduces a novel, cost-effective EL imaging solution using a modified consumer camera. The findings highlight the efficacy of EL imaging in detecting an array of solar cell defects, underscored by the affordability of the setup. The accessible and cost-friendly nature of the EL methodology offers a promising inspection alternative for small to medium-sized PV systems, marking a significant stride in PV inspection innovations.

articleTitle: Review of the Technology and Problems Faced by Electric Vehicles Drive Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The use of fossil fuels in transportation systems is the second-largest contributor to the production of greenhouse gases. Electric vehicles, also known as EVs, are widely considered to be an excellent answer to this issue. Due to the fact that the propeller is propelled by an electric motor as opposed to an internal combustion engine, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions can be reduced by the EVs. When combined with renewable energy sources, EVs could enable zero-emission transportation. This study reviews the developments of EVs in terms of battery technology trends, charging methods, as well as new research challenges. The aim is to provide an overview of the most recent advancements in the constantly evolving field of electric vehicles. In a comparison study that looks at specific energy and power, cost, and application. Batteries are employed as the major energy storage. This study helps us better grasp the present status of battery technology used in electric vehicles (EVs).

articleTitle: Dental Imaging Using a Higher Signal-to-Noise Ratio Optical Coherence Tomography System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents an optical coherence tomography (OCT) system in conjunction with a novel image reconstruction technique employed for in vitro imaging of human teeth. The primary goal is to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the obtained images. The study entails a comparative analysis between the conventional Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) OCT image reconstruction method and a newly introduced scaled nonuniform discrete Fourier transform (NDFT) approach. The findings reveal that the NDFT method consistently delivers superior results in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and overall image quality, even when dealing with redundant and nonuniform frequency domain samples. In light of these results, this paper concludes that integrating NDFT into OCT procedures has the potential to significantly enhance the quality of image reconstructions, thereby fostering its broader application in the field of dental imaging.

articleTitle: Predicting the Risk of Diabetes Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Diabetes is a metabolic condition depicted by elevated blood glucose levels where the pancreas is unable to generate adequate insulin or the body is incapable of utilizing insulin properly, thus incapable to transport the glucose into the cells for energy. Prompt diagnosis and treatment, more particularly lifestyle modification, can avert or delay the emergence of microvascular and macrovascular complications. The aim of the study is to predict the risk of developing diabetes using a variety of machine learning classification algorithms applied on a publicly available diabetes dataset as well as to investigate the impact of the feature selection techniques and class imbalance handling method on the predictive power of these models The model with the best performance was achieved by random forest with synthetic minority oversampling method and without any feature selection technique with an area under the curve of 0.983, 99% accuracy, 100% recall, 100% precision and 100%. Moreover, a simple web-based application that predicts risk of acquiring diabetes was also developed as a decision support tool. It was also integrated with explainable artificial intelligence method to highlight the characteristics leading towards the prediction decision of the model. Prompt and accurate diabetes recognition can assist patients to foresightedly incorporate lifestyle habit modifications so as to ward off risks of complications of uncontrolled diabetes.

articleTitle: Delay Compensation in the PMSM Control System by Using Predictive-PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Based on the positive outcomes of using PI-type controllers in PMSM (Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor) control systems, this paper introduces an extension of this controller type, namely Predictive-PI, to compensate for delays in the control system during sensor readings and computational effects involved in control algorithms and state observers. This extended controller offers a lower complexity suitable for real-time applications. The structure of the initial PI controller is improved by predicting the order size at the current time using the information given by the controller commands over the previous time interval equal to the delay, which is a predictive PI type controller. The structure and equations for a predictive PI controller are presented, along with numerical simulations for different delay values. The predictive PI controller demonstrates effective control performance and maintains a low complexity control algorithm, making it well-suited for real-time implementations.

articleTitle: Comparison of 2L and 3L-NPC Power Converter-Based a Level-2 Isolated Off-Board Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper presents an off-board charger system for any electric vehicle based on a single-stage power converter operation that performs as a three-phase pulse width modulation rectifier. To enhance the safety issue by itself, a step-down transformer with galvanic isolation is added. Additionally, the off-board charger system allows bidirectional power flow in both grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid operations. To analyze this system, only G2V operation is shown by comparing a two-level power converter charger with a three-level neutral point clamped power converter charger. In light of its controller, the off-board charger is designed to charge a battery in constant current and constant voltage mode in compliance with Level 2 of charging power. Based on this controller, it can support grid power quality under a unity power factor. Simulation-based verification is conducted on a maximum power rating of 22 kW to claim the performance of steady-state operation and dynamic operation.

Author Keywords: three-level neutral point clamped power converter

articleTitle: Harmonic Utilization Permanent Magnet Topology Design Considerations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Reducing costly permanent magnet material while increasing torque density is of great interest. A Harmonic Utilization Permanent Magnet (HUPM) machine topology, proposed in recent literature, offers the same torque density for reduced magnet utilization. However, adoption of the HUPM topology requires understanding for selection of feasible design parameters. This paper proposes an analytical technique for calculating the design parameters as well as considerations for the adoption of the HUPM topology. The analytical technique is applied to test the validity and delineate challenges associated with adoption of HUPM. Finite element analysis confirms the design considerations required for successful adoption of the HUPM topology.

articleTitle: Towards a Hierarchical and Distributed Power Management Framework for SGs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Escalating global power(energy) demands and the need to avail it in a reliable, efficient manner has led to the modernization of legacy and current power system grids into Smart Grid (SGs) equivalents his article proposes a hierarchical distributed arc. The paper mitigates the advantages of both hierarchical and distributed architectures in Smart Grid management and control. As is known, a hierarchical architecture of control and management will facilitate massive-scale data acquisition, exchanges, processing, and control for cooperative power exchanges between prosumers (end users), and the main power grid, via cloud computing. Such a distributed architecture affords autonomous decision-making capabilities with agent-based intelligence through edge/fog computing. Analytical results show substantial achievements of the proposed hierarchical and distributed SG/MG management framework based on an actual protocol and system implementation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Power Generation Between Concentrated Solar Power and Photovoltaic Systems Under High Altitude Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Solar energy harnessed through Photovoltaic (PV) systems and Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems represents two distinct technological with high potential. This article undertakes a comparative analysis of these power generation technologies within one of the globe's most radiant solar zones: The Andean region of Bolivia, also distinguished by its elevated altitudes. The evaluation revolves around the specifications requirement for a 50 MW plant situated in Bolivia's La Paz department. The evaluation criteria include the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE), Plant Factor (PF), Investment Cost (IC), and land area requirements. Moreover, considering the intermittent nature of solar energy, this study also compares the energy storage capabilities inherent to both technologies. Additionally, comparisons of the results were made with analogous CSP installations located in Italy, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: A New Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna for Millimeter Wave Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The use of wireless devices and wireless technology has increased extraordinarily during recent times. Along with the usage, the demands to send more data in less time are on the rise. Millimeter wave (mmWave) technology is a possible solution to such demands. This paper discusses millimeter wave (mmWave) technology and antennas that have been recently designed and developed for 60 GHz wireless communications. Also, a novel patch antenna with capacitive feeding is proposed. The antenna is dual polarized. This characteristic is acheived by using two orthogonal feeds; for linear and circular polarizations. This antenna works well from 57–63 GHz thus covering the 6 GHz ISM band. The reflection coefficient values are well below -10dB for the whole 6 GHz band. The mutual coupling values are below -25dB. The total efficiency is about 86%. For comparison, a dual-polarized antenna with inset feeding is also designed and simulated. The simulations are done in CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Effect of Geometric Nodes Distribution on Performance of Wireless Body Area Network in Wearable Jackets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Wireless Body area networks (WBANs) and wearable sensing materials are at the forefront of advanced wireless and health care, military, and industrial applications for the purpose of monitoring and support. The objective of this work is to present designs with analysis of effect of node placement and distribution on energy consumption and path loss parameters. These parameters affect communication channel properties and energy source lifetime. As it is critical to preserve energy, which is related to path loss coefficient, the work shows that the Back-to-Back V-Shape without center nodes design is a more efficient design in terms of energy consumption and path loss effect. Such a design is more stable as a result of supporting nodes. The 16-node WBAN covers a wearable jacket of 1m by 0.5 m dimension. The work also emphasize the importance of jacket materials, by simulation using three different path loss coefficients. In addition, the work shows that data delivery effectiveness is affected by the way nodes are placed.

articleTitle: Face to Face Augmented Reality - Broadening the Horizons of AR Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: When users wear Augmented Reality (AR) Head Mounted Displays (HMDs), they occlude most parts of the face. While body language is crucial in effective team communication and negotiation tactics, the effect of eye contact and facial expressions cannot be neglected. However, the degree to which users in AR environments can expressively interact with each other is hindered by HMDs which occlude a large portion of the face and do not realistically blend with the terrain surroundings. Recent developments generate highly photorealistic avatars in Virtual Reality (VR) but they do not solve a multitude of questions which include blending of the virtual model in an AR setting, real-time performance along with high fidelity of temporal coherence as well estimation of high-resolution outputs. We propose to develop a technique for enabling natural and expressive face-to-face communication between subjects in AR environments by removing the HMD barrier where the virtual environments blend seamlessly with a photorealistic face model.

articleTitle: A Data Driven Approach to Process Control Modelling Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The optimization of process control loops has long been a critical aspect of industrial operations. In recent years, the landscape of process optimization has witnessed significant advancements driven by the integration of machine learning and artificial intelligence technologies. These innovations have opened new avenues to enhance model performance and accuracy, offering opportunities to revolutionize traditional optimization approaches. Traditionally, process optimization has adhered to well-established frameworks and methodologies. However, the rapid evolution and diversification of available tools and techniques have ushered in a transformative era. Despite the proven effectiveness of conventional methods, they often fall short in harnessing critical benefits, such as reduced processing time and enhanced efficiency. This paper advocates for exploring alternative approaches to process optimization by harnessing readily available machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques, which have the potential to deliver expedited and precise results using operational data. These advanced models meticulously analyze process data and are rigorously evaluated, allowing for a direct comparison with existing optimization results. Consequently, this comparison aids in the identification of the most suitable model for the given process. As a result, the proposed model not only achieves heightened accuracy but also facilitates improved feature engineering. This leads to better control and enhanced product quality, ultimately driving increased production efficiency and profitability. By embracing the evolving landscape of process optimization, industries can remain competitive and adaptive in today's dynamic manufacturing environments.

articleTitle: Electricity Cost Minimization for A Low-Income Household: A South African Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The recent economic trajectory in South Africa has impacted many low-income household families. This has been because of high inflation, load-shedding, and unemployment. Many families are enabled to afford the cost of electricity. This further deteriorates the liberation of the majority in the country. In this paper, a technique based on genetic algorithm (GA) for a hybrid energy system for cost minimization is proposed. The technique is aimed at minimizing the cost of electricity by optimization the operation use of both the photovoltaic (PV) solar and wind energy (WE) systems tied into the power distribution grid. The results obtained show that by using the GA technique for optimizing the operation a decrease of 48.8% in summer and 35.6% in winter was achieved.

articleTitle: Optimal Selection of Switch Model Parameters for ADC-Based Full-Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The incorporation of real-time Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) simulators has become one of the pillars of the power electronics control design cycle. This integration is necessary to verify the effectiveness of controller implementations. Despite the rapid evolution in FPGA devices' computational capacity employed by Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) tools, developers are consistently faced with the need to strike a balance between acceptable accuracy and the practicality of implementing models and techniques. The methodology presented in this paper is for implementing a full-bridge converter using the Associate Discrete Circuit (ADC) model, specifically designed for real-time simulator applications. Furthermore, this study presents a novel methodology for parameter selection of (ADC) parameters utilizing the Artificial Bee Colony algorithm (ABC). The utilization of the ADC-based model facilitates the establishment of a uniform converter topology during simulation, irrespective of the switch states. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the introduced methodology in selecting optimal parameters for an ADC switch-based full-bridge converter, reducing overshoot in the converter's output voltage and current.

articleTitle: Model Based Development Methodology in Compliance with ISO 26262 for Safe Automotive ECU
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This work presents a practical approach of designing a functionally safe ECU for automotive application by implementing the Model Based Development (MBD) methodology. Functional safety (FuSa) in automotive can be achieved by strictly following the processes of electrical and electronic systems development as given in the ISO 26262. The scope of FuSa encompasses the risks emerging from systematic failures and random hardware failures. One approach to mitigate these failures is the Model Based Development (MBD) on which the ISO 26262 provides guidance. This approach enables to model an ECU and accelerates an IP creation by automatic RTL code generation for rapid prototyping on an FPGA level. In this work the MBD is implemented in accordance to the ISO 26262 to design and test a hardware model of an embedded ECU. The embedded Design under Test (DUT) is simulated and its output verified in Matlab/Simulink. Upon successful results, the RTL codes of the DUT are generated for a target FPGA. The RTL codes are simulated and the functionality of the DUT is verified at the FPGA level.

articleTitle: Effects of Blade Pitch on the Power Generation of a Novel 3D-Printed Cascaded Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of various Wind Turbine blade pitch angles on the electrical power generation capability of a Dual-Rotor Cascaded Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine (Cascaded HAWT). It aims to (1) examine the overall structure of two different small-scale 3D-Printed Wind Turbines; one single-rotor “Control” HAWT meant to represent a typical commercial Wind Turbine, and one Dual-Rotor Cascaded HAWT, (2) analyze the electrical power output of the Control HAWT compared to the electrical power output of the Dual-Rotor Cascaded HAWT, and (3) assess methods to improve the Dual-Rotor Cascaded HAWT's electric power generation capabilities on a commercial scale.

articleTitle: Development of Phylum Chordata Sound Recognition System using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques: A Case Study of Catfish
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Sound recognition refers to the technology or process of identifying and classifying different sounds or audio signals. This study aims to develop a sound recognition system using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques to classify and identify the gender of catfish based on their speech patterns. The study explores a range of supervised ML and DL algorithms, such as the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Naïve Bayes (NB), and others, to predict the gender of catfish. The extracted features from the audio signals of the catfish serve as inputs to these algorithms, which produce binary predictions classifying the catfish samples as either male or female. This study further explores data analysis of the audio signals from the male and female catfish. The automated sound recognition system proves to be a more efficient and accurate approach compared to traditional methods, which rely on time-consuming visual observations. Evaluation metrics such as Accuracy, Sensitivity, and more, were employed to gauge the effectiveness of the algorithms in predicting the gender of catfish based on speech patterns. Among the employed algorithms, ANN and NB demonstrate the highest accuracy, achieving a score of 89.47%.

articleTitle: Python-Based Simulation of Non-Gaussian Stationary Random Process with Arbitrary Auto-Correlation Function
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Simulation of stationary random processes (time series) is an essential engineering tool for system prototyping, design, and optimization. To create a simulation, a randomly generated time series must have a pre-defined distribution and autocorrelation function (ACF). It is challenging to model non-Gaussian distributions as using a linear filter can alter the target distribution. To address this issue, we wrote a Python package that implements one of the prominent methods in the field of random process simulation. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first publicly available implementation of such a simulator in Python.

articleTitle: A Constrained Two-Link Brachiating Robot for Power Line Inspection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper introduces a cascaded control approach for a fully actuated two-link brachiating powerline inspection robot. The robot operates under the constraints of internal and external factors such as friction and wind drag. The control system combines Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Computed Torque Control (CTC) techniques to achieve precise control. The robot's mechanical design is created using SolidWorks, transformed into a Matlab Simulink environment. An optimal trajectory is generated through the use of MATLAB's optimization toolbox. The control architecture, leveraging the robot's actuation capabilities, effectively tracks trajectories while maintaining stability. It also compensates for internal constraints and mitigates external disturbances imposed on the Simulink model. The effectiveness of this control approach is demonstrated through simulations within the Simulink environment and visualization facilitated by SimScape multibody simulation. This study represents a significant advancement in the integration of mechanical CAD models and symbolic tools with SimScape, potentially contributing to the process of control system development by reducing the complexity of equation derivation and approximation techniques.

articleTitle: Modeling and Forecasting Photovoltaic Power Production
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As the world's population grows, there is a need to find new sources of energy that are more sustainable. Photovoltaic (PV) energy is one of the renewable energy sources (RES) expected to have the greatest margin for growth in the near future. Given their intermittency, RES bring uncertainty and instability to the management of the power system, therefore it is essential to predict their behavior for different time frames. This paper aims to find the most effective forecasting method for PV energy production that could be applied to different time frames. PV energy production is directly dependent on solar radiation and temperature. Several forecasting approaches are proposed in this paper. A multiple linear regression (MLR) model is proposed to predict the monthly energy production based on the climatic parameters of the previous year. Different approaches are proposed based on first predicting the temperature and radiation and then applying the PV mathematical models to predict the produced energy. Three methods are proposed to predict the climatic parameters: using the average values, the additive decomposition, or the Holt-Winters method. Comparing the errors of the four proposed forecasting methods, the best model is the Holt-Winters, which presents smaller errors for radiation, temperature, and produced energy. This method is close to additive decomposition.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of High-Voltage Transformers with Different Powers and Insulation Conditions Using the FDS Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article deals with the analysis of the comparison of different transformers with different performances and qualities of insulation properties at the same indoor temperature and the analysis of the insulation properties of the transformer at different temperatures by the method of frequency dielectric spectroscopy (FDS). The advantage of determining the insulation state of the transformer using the capacity by the FDS method is a smaller temperature dependence compared to the loss factor, which was verified during the analysis of the effect of temperature. The disadvantage of determining the insulation condition of the transformer using the capacity was the influence of the geometric arrangement of the insulation, i.e. depending on the type and performance of the machine.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and Classification of Cardiac Arrhythmias Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Cardiac arrhythmia stands as a prominent contributor to cardiovascular diseases, resulting in significant global mortality rates. The methods for diagnosing diseases, including cardiovascular conditions, through the processing of biomedical signals, continuously advance and develop over time. The progress in signal processing techniques has enabled the extraction of various types of information from Electrocardiography (ECG) signals. The manual analysis of ECG signals is very difficult because of its complexity. However, the use of artificial intelligence algorithms simplifies this process. In this study, we used a convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm that mainly facilitates the categorization of the type of arrhythmia and reduces the time of this process. The dataset used in this study is MIT-BIH arrhythmia which is widely popular among scientists from this field. 4 classes were chosen in this classification: N, SVEB, VEB, and F. As a result, the overall classification accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of the proposed approach are 99.24%, 99.24%, and 96.94% respectively. The obtained outcomes are being evaluated against the highest-level or pioneering norms within the discipline.

articleTitle: Implementation and Use of Clinical Decision Support System in Malawi National ART EMR System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The introduction of Malawi national antiretroviral therapy (NART) electronic medical record (EMR) system has improved the management and reporting of ART patient data. Designed to aid in decision-making by providers for individual patients in their care, the system has been integrated with a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS). NART EMR system was introduced in 2006, and by 2021, it had been extended to over 206 healthcare facilities in the country. Despite several evaluations conducted on the NART EMR, there has been limited attention given to evaluating the implementation and usage of the CDSS within the NART EMR system. Hence, the study sought to establish how CDSS in the NART EMR system has been implemented and used by healthcare providers in Malawi to improve decision making on an individual patient on antiretroviral therapy (ART) at any point in time. The study employed a qualitative methodology, gathering data through observations, interviews, and an in-depth analysis of the system. The study establishes that smooth integration of CDSS in EMR system into regular and normal clinical workflow contributes to the success of CDSS use. Despite the successes of CDSS in EMR system, issues of system quality and information quality must be addressed during design and implementation of the CDSS to enhance efficiency and effectiveness of the system. The study suggests that those responsible for implementation should prioritize improving the underlying logic of the clinical decision support intervention in order to address existing concerns and improve the accuracy of the provided information. Additionally, the study recommends active consultation with the system's real users during the implementation process.

articleTitle: Voltage Fluctuation Correction for Renewable Energy Systems in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Renewable energies are becoming an important element of modern society, but integration into the power grid poses critical challenges. Power quality is an important aspect when integrating renewable energy. The main power quality concerns are 1) Voltage and frequency fluctuations caused by uncontrollable fluctuations in renewable energy sources. The variable nature of renewable energy sources due to constantly changing weather conditions results in voltage and frequency fluctuations in interconnected grids. 2) Harmonics introduced by power electronics equipment used to generate renewable energy. If the penetration rate of renewable energy is high, the effects of harmonics can be significant. This article comprehensively reviews the new power quality challenges of integrating renewable energies. It summarizes wind turbines and PV systems, their power quality issues, and existing approaches to improving power quality. A method is reviewed, and the control technology-based power quality improvement proposed using a voltage restorer. Future research directions are thus recommended based on the result shown in this paper and thereby help to mitigate power quality challenges for renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Optimising the Quantity of Fiber in an FTTH/GPON network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The telecommunications access network is undergoing profound change, with twisted-pair cables being replaced by optical fiber cables, which offer exceptional bandwidth. The incumbent operators, owners of vast civil engineering networks, are favouring FTTH/GPON technology, using their GIS (Geographic Information System) databases to deploy optical fiber cables. This article takes a look at the engineering of FTTH/GPON (Fiber To The Home/Gigabit-Passive Optical Network) technology and proposes the use of mathematical tools to optimise the quantity of optical fiber cables to be deployed.

articleTitle: Design of a Reconfigurable Superdirective Antenna for Wi-Fi Module
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper is a model of a reconfigurable superdirective antennas. The array antennas is made for Wi-Fi module in 2.45GHz ISM band. Monopoles, two-by-two linear and 0.1λ spaced, set on a Fr4 substrate respecting 40mm radius of a circular Wi-Fi module. Differents configurations are established with passive components directly integrated to antennas with pin diodes. The obtained results show that properly integrated, array antennas can maintain compared to simulation a reconfigurable superdirectivity with a gain in order of 5.2dB in four directions of azimutal plane and significantly increase its radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: An Automated System for Detecting and Preventing Phishing Attempts on Steam Accounts
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In recent years Steam has become a giant in the gaming industry. The Valve-owned digital distribution platform held an estimated 75% of market share in 2013, and continues to grow. However, with such a large user base comes the ever-increasing threat of security breaches in both the Steam database and individual Steam user accounts. While Steam does make use of a mobile authentication app, users are still susceptible to malware and/or phishing attempts that can cause users to lose access to their accounts through manipulation or gaining access to recovery email accounts. This project aims to investigate how the authentication process can be improved or if a solution can be created to help prevent the worst-case scenario when users become victims of phishing attacks.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz Microstrip Antenna Array for Future Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this article, a microstrip patch antenna array has been designed for sub-terahertz application. The designed antenna array consists of four rectangular-shaped radiating patches which are fed using the microstrip line feeding technique. The dielectric material utilized as a substrate is Roger RO3010 which has an epsilon value of 11.2, responsible for compact antenna size, it also exhibits minimal energy absorption and dissipation. The designed antenna has achieved acceptable simulated results of important parameters which include radiation pattern, Gain, and return loss, Bandwidth, current distribution, and impedance matching of the antenna. The designed antenna array offers increased bandwidth, enabling higher data rates and ultra-low latency. The proposed Sub-terahertz antenna array can support the deployment of high-speed, low-latency wireless networks for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), autonomous vehicles, and smart cities.

articleTitle: Electronic and Mechanical Design of an Exoskeletal Structure Prototype to Contribute to Partial Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This research develops a proposal for the mechanical and electronic design of an exoskeleton type robotic prototype that aims to contribute to the partial rehabilitation of the hand through muscle sensors (EMG), to detect the patient's intention to move and achieve an adequate rehabilitation routine, the development methodology is based on three stages. The first stage is the electronics where the control circuit is developed and the simulation of the muscle sensors (EMG) for the activation of the linear actuators, in this stage a motion registration circuit is also developed that is reflected on an LCD screen, The second stage is the mechanics that studies the biomechanics of the hand for the creation of the design of the links of the external and internal phalanges generating the extension and flexion of the fingers of the mechanism, and the third stage is the integration of the mechanical and electronic system that describes all the components that make up the system. The simulation of the Von Mises stress analysis in the SolidWorks software with the PET type plastic composite material was obtained as results, the parts of the exoskeleton withstood the applied loads, maintaining that the prototype design has the ability to hold and support the fingers.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Resonant LLC Power Converter for Battery Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper examines the basic principle, design and modeling of converter for wide variation of supply voltage as well as wide variation of output load current. Appropriate controller can be selected such that output can be regulated, then the efficiency can be improved, stress on the devices can also be reduced to minimal. The potential choice for controlling output voltage using a fuzzy logic controller in comparison with PI controller is also explained in this paper. The benefits and drawbacks of both the techniques are evaluated. Simulations are carried out for wide variation of supply voltage as well as wide variation of load current in order to verify the theoretical analysis of resonant converter.

articleTitle: Analytical and Numerical Modeling of the Thermal Performance of 3D System-in-Package (SiP)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The study will investigate the heat dissipation capabilities of three-dimensional (3D) stacked System-in-Package (SiP) configurations using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations for heat transfer analysis (HTA). The model introduced in this paper will be utilized to assess the thermal viability boundaries of 3D electronics and to pinpoint necessary enhancements to conventional packaging methods for accommodating functional 3D-SiPs effectively. By employing the finite element method (FEM) in combination with COMSOL Multiphysics® software, both modeling and simulation processes will be executed to verify heat dissipation pathways, aiming to reinforce the thermal performance of 3D-SiP assemblies. The investigation will primarily consider the impact of distinct geometrical attributes and thermophysical characteristics on the heat dissipation capabilities of SiPs. The investigation's results, which reduced the maximum temperature within the SiP by 84 %, could serve as an essential foundation for the development of thermal design guidelines specifically adapted to 3D-SiPs. In so doing, they would make a significant contribution to the skilful reinforcement of thermal management strategies.

articleTitle: Implementing Machine Learning Strategies to Evaluate Analytical Algorithm for Unsupervised Narratives Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As electronic records overwhelm across the web these days, the content extraction field is gaining prominence and is being employed extensively. Narratives pieces, which might be summarized in an extracting manner devoid losing their deeper significance, are a key electronic material utilized by individuals taking competitive assessments. We are attempting to create a method that might help learners in extracting current information from narratives in a shorter length of time. The contrasting analysis among two modern and sophisticated procedures is accomplished in order to highlight the superior one. The extractive summarization is carried out utilizing three distinct Text Ranking algorithm procedures, summaries functioning, proportion, and word count. This study focuses on the analysis of the outcomes that were obtained with the utilization of extractive and unsupervised summarization. The aim of the current work is the analysis of outcomes obtained through the Text-Rank methodology utilizing the Gensim Environment with the ROUGE approach.

articleTitle: Inherent Biolectrical Circuits in Neural Synapse
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper proposes the idea that neural synapse is a pure electrical event. In order to derive this the well-known Fokker-Planck equation is employed. Basically the process of synapse is divided in three phases: (i) The transit of synaptic vesicles to the axon zone, (ii) the releasing of neurotransmitters in the cleft zone, and (iii) the transfer of neurotransmitters to the adjacent neuron through the ion channels. The dynamics equation is expressed as function of the volumetric charge density. Once the electrical variables have been defined the respective permittivities are associated to each zone where exists transit of neurotransmitters. The time derivative of resulting electric charge is interpreted as the current that is created by the pass of neurotransmitters from a neuron to another in full concordance to the current concepts of synapse. Indeed, under the present treatment is is possible to identify the cases where exists accumulation of neurotransmitters along the cleft zone, fact that would suggest the idea that the obstruction of neurotransmitters breaks down synapse. Therefore, such blocking might be well related to neurological diseases. Analysis of the created currents are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of all Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cell Employing Ga2O3 and CuSCN Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of the performance of CsPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) through rigorous numerical simulations. We explore a range of inorganic materials to assess their suitability for use as hole transport layers (HTL) and electron transport layers (ETL). The ETL candidates considered encompass ZnO, Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and PCBM, while our evaluation for potential HTL materials includes NIO, CuSCN, CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and Spiro-OMeTAD. Our research highlights the superiority of CsPbI3-based PSCs when employing Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the ETL and CuSCN as the HTL, surpassing the performance of other solar cell combinations. The optimized solar cell exhibits exceptional characteristics, including a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{SC}$</tex> of 16.76 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{OC}$</tex> of 1.13 V, FF of 87.82%, and an impressive efficiency of 16.62%. These findings hold substantial promise for guiding the development of high-performance, all-inorganic CsPbI3 PSCs.

articleTitle: Molecular Communications as Quantum Mechanics Coherent States
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In most cases, molecular communication might require of wavefront-like dynamics that maximizes the arrival of drug into a target. Thus, while the technique of drug delivery can partially see as a stochastic dynamics, one might to expect that certainly probabilistic theories can be applied successfully. In this letter, the theory of quantum mechanics coherent states is used to calculate the success probability of engineered cell communications. The resulting probabilities are compared to the ones obtained without probabilistic approaches, showing that the quantum theory turns out to be precise, fact that would open space to speculate that molecular communication can be inherently described by Quantum coherent states.

articleTitle: Analysis of Baseline Security Standards and Predictive Analytics for Cyber Supply Chain Attacks and Artificial Neural Network as a Proposed Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Supply chain attacks remain one of the industry's most sophisticated and costly threats. The intrusion of the vendor's network leads to the exposure of critical Infrastructure and the disruption of services. Attacks such as Distributed Denial of Service and Malware attacks like Ransomware among others. This research paper evaluates the nature of supply chain attacks and the existing gaps in prevention and deterrence of these attacks. This paper is focused on applying predictive mechanisms using Artificial Intelligence at the gateway of the intended target infrastructure. The paper also assesses the state of preparedness by the National Institute of Science and Technology (NIST) Risk Management against Supply Chain attacks and the joint preventive roles that suppliers and clients can coordinate as a response to the supply chain attack. Recommendations for deterrence are highlighted in the evaluation's findings. This study proposes the use of artificial neural networks to build highly effective models that can detect software supply chain attacks based on set metrics on software supply chain network characteristics.

articleTitle: Sense Amplifier Offset Error Correction Method for High Speed Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The offset error correction method for high-speed systems is presented. In high-speed systems comparator offset variation becomes more important. This variation has an impact on the proper work of the calibration blocks. The proposed method corrects offset error of sense amplifier through hysteresis to provide precious value of output stage and avoid functional fails. The offset of comparator is critical in many systems such as Double Data Rate (DDR) and can cause slew rate mismatch by generating incorrect slew rate code through finite state machine (FSM). The proposed architecture can be used in high-speed systems where data rates are 10Gbps or higher. Modern high-speed systems require less than 2mV offset and proposed method can be used in special input/output circuits of several standards such as Double Data Rate (DDR), Universal Serial Bus (USB) and Peripheral Component Interconnect (PCI).

articleTitle: Methodology for Measuring and Improving Inter-Organizational Interoperability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Interoperability is a constantly evolving field, particularly with the development of connected and intelligent devices. Numerous methods have been developed to assess interoperability, based on maturity models. However, with the evolution of technology, the development of the Internet, connectivity is no longer a real problem, and isolated systems are becoming increasingly rare. Improving interoperability is therefore no longer oriented towards interconnection, but rather towards optimizing business processes. Activities generated by interoperability are a priori considered to be of no value compared with business activities and contribute to putting data into the right format for transmission or use. This study proposes a methodology for assessing interoperability based on data exchanged between systems. The use of the proposed Data Circuit based on generation and integration processes makes it possible to identify points of improvement of the business process to have data produced in a format that requires the least processing before its use, especially in the context of the execution of a process instance.

articleTitle: Neural-Gradient Maximum Power Point Tracking Method for Solar Panel
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: A popular method used to maximize the power output of solar panels is Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). This work attempted to improve MPPT by utilizing an artificial neural network (ANN) algorithm and gradient perturbation of the duty cycle, dubbed the Neural-Gradient MPPT method. The ANN takes in as input, irradiance, and temperature, whereas its outputs are the power and current at the MPP. We compared our proposed algorithm to the popular traditional MPPT algorithm, Perturb and Observe (P&O). Our proposed MPPT technique has a faster response to abrupt changes in solar irradiance and temperature and less steady-state error than the baseline P&O algorithm.

articleTitle: Free Space Optical Communication Link Performance Based on Various Transmission Schemes Over Gamma-Gamma Distribution Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Due to massive growth in telecommunication systems, the required services such as reliable quality of service, secured connectivity, and low cost of technology by the users have always been a major concern that requires attention. Free space optical systems have recently been known to be an option that can proffer solutions to these problems. However, these systems rely on atmospheric weather which is prone to several degradations. This study assesses how different modulation methods perform on free space optics using the gamma-gamma channel model to determine the feasibility of the systems' communication link performance. The results show an increase in the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) with a decrease in the average bit error rate (BER). Based on the analytical results at the highest link range of 5200, the received bit error rate of BPSK, DPSK, and OOK was about 0.048, 0.060, and 0.140 observed at the strong fading strength when at an average SNR of 30 dB. It was deducted that the system performance degrades as the strength of channel fading fluctuates between weak, moderate, and strong levels of turbulence.

articleTitle: Gateways Placement Optimization in Wireless Mesh Networks with Interference and QoS Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Wireless Mesh Networks (WMNs) consist of mesh clients, routers, and gateways. Gateways, directly linked to wired infrastructure, serve as Internet-connected routers. In WMNs, client nodes use the wired setup for data transfer including web content, emails, audio, and video. Due to mixed wired and wireless interfaces, gateways are complex and costly to set up and maintain. Strategic gateway placing is pivotal in WMN design, defining network performance. Each gateway's placement carries significant implications, molding network behavior. Adding gateways increases costs due to higher expenses, while reducing them heightens latency and decreases data throughput. Multiple strategies address gateway placement in WMNs, including iterative greedy algorithms, augmenting algorithms, and game theory-based methods. Despite potential advantages, these techniques encounter limitations, particularly in ensuring Quality of Service (QoS) measures such as network throughput, end-to-end delay, and relay load. Addressing these challenges, we propose the Rec-GT algorithm, combining weighted recursive techniques and graph theory to optimize gateway placement. This integration aims to enhance network throughput, reduce end-to-end delay, and minimize relay load. Our Rec-GT algorithm aims for superior gateway positioning performance. We plan to validate its efficacy through simulations and performance comparisons, evaluating network throughput, end-to-end delay, and relay load on the MATLAB platform.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sensorless Control Methods of PMSM Ship Propulsion Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) play a major role in large electric transportation such as electric ships. This is due to its high efficiency and high torque density. For these large propulsion drive applications, high quality sensorless control is preferred since the reliability and safety are important considerations. In this paper the methods and performances of different observers for sensorless control of large ship-propulsion PMSM drives are compared. The observers are compared with each other to provide insightful information for the purpose of selecting the most suitable observer technique for implementation in PMSM ship propulsion. In this regard the sliding mode observer (SMO), the model reference adaptive system (MRAS) observer, the Luenberger observer and the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) are applied for sensorless control. The MATLAB-simulation results of these observers for a 4-MW ship-propulsion PMSM are provided. The results show that the SMO has excellent dynamic performance compared to the other observers at both low and high machine speeds.

articleTitle: Reusing Outputs from S-Boxes for Tamper Resistant Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: AES is currently a standard cryptographic algorithm widely used on the Internet. During the AES process, there is a non-linear operation called the S-box. This S-box is not only utilized for encryption but also finds in cryptographic hash. The only difference between cryptographic hashing and pseudorandomness is the preservation of determinism and the guarantee of the longest possible period. In this paper, we propose a countermeasure against power analysis attacks by exploiting the output of the inherent S-box in AES and utilizing it as a source of randomness.

articleTitle: An Electronically Tunable Capacitance Multiplier Structure Using DTMOS Technique for the Low Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this study, a capacitor multiplier based on Multiple Output-Voltage Difference Transconductance Amplifier (MO-VDTA) is built by employing DTMOS transistors. The proposed MO-VDTA based capacitor multiplier is composed of three stages, one of which is operated in the subthreshold region. The proposed structure works with ±0.9V and ±0.3V supply voltages and can be safely tunable for the low frequency operations where the large capacitor values are needed. The proposed multiplier is tested in a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order low-pass filter, while the cut-off frequency of proposed filter from “12Hz” up to “40Hz” and total power consumption of the proposed filter is given around 700µW. Also, multiplication factor can be changed from “40000” to “120000” by the virtue of bias currents. In order to verify the multiplier performance, Monte-Carlo, THD and noise analysis are given in conjunction with the filter results. Performance comparison with the previous studies is presented as well.

Author Keywords: Multiple Output Voltage Differencing Transconductance Amplifier (MO-VDTA)

articleTitle: Holistic Monitoring: Advanced Metrics for Heterogeneous Industrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Holistic monitoring focuses on the health of heterogeneous industrial networks incorporating Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN). A centralized configuration approach, commonly referred to as Centralized User Configuration and Centralized Network Controller, is commonly employed for industrial networks that feature TSN. The continuous monitoring of network health with the current configuration improves enforcement efficiency and is a major concern for industrial users. Overprovisioning, increased network management complexity, and difficulties integrating new applications are some of the obstacles in heterogeneous networks. After providing an overview of the corresponding research, this paper presents advanced metrics for assessing the healthiness of heterogeneous industrial networks.

articleTitle: Viewer Perception Analysis of Video Collaboration of the Nihongo Mantappu YouTube Channel Using Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: YouTube is an online video-sharing platform, one of the YouTube channels with collaborative content with the highest number of subscribers in Indonesia is the Nihongo Mantappu channel. This study uses the aspect-based sentiment analysis method for content development to analyze audience perceptions of collaborative video comments from the Nihongo Mantappu channel. The aspect used in this study is the type of content consisting of Cooking, Challenge, Education, Mukbang, QnA, and Vlog content. The Decision Tree model, with a sentiment analysis accuracy rate of 96.08% and aspect-based settlement analysis of 98.36%, shows that the overall proportion of sentiment is dominated by neutral sentiment with a percentage of 60.5%, positive sentiment with a percentage of 23.8%, and negative sentiment with a percentage of 15.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>• The results of this study can be used as a reference in developing collaborative video content on the Nihongo Mantappu channel.

articleTitle: Proposed a Solution Based on Functional Dependency Graphs for Transactional Fact Table Error Correction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Process mining refers to the set of techniques used to mine the event logs of process-oriented information systems that manage and execute processes to gain hidden knowledge about an organization's actual business processes. Data warehouses are a form of database that stores data from different sources. Data warehouses contain three types of tables: transactional fact table, periodic fact table, and cumulative fact table. The transactional fact table, contains a frequent error in the mapping between the primary key, cumulative fact table measure and dimension level granularity. This paper proposed a solution based on functional dependency graphs to correct the frequent errors in the transactional fact table.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Fields and Health Impacts- An Overview of the Literature
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMFs) are ubiquitous anthropogenic physical stressors that are rapidly expanding. Humans are mainly exposed from a multitude of RF-EMF energy emitting sources. Several studies suggest an association between RF-EMFs exposure and development of health induced outcomes such as cancer and other severe effects. This paper discusses the association between RF-EMF exposure and severe health implications. Relevant literature was searched using Google Scholar, PubMed, NCBI Science Direct, and Research Gate. Out of a total of fifty articles, thirty-nine were selected and used to compile this review. Study findings were compared with each other based on possible health effects related to RF-EMF exposure. Fewer studies suggest that the RF-EMF exposure be classified as a Group 1 known human carcinogen.
