Furthermore, highlights the advantages of simulation modeling in supply chain management, including the ability to capture real-time data, simulate multiple scenarios, and evaluate the impact of different strategies on performance metrics. This simulation framework will help to model the supply chain operation of multiple dairy products for period of eight weeks, including varying demand and supply for different products which differ across the US region. It will allow us to provide insights for the future by capturing real data with abrupt changes in demand at the plant level. A comparative study on total cost (Fixed cost + Transportation cost) across the plant with and without optimization at different scenarios is presented for better realization of ease in making decisions at the business level. Holistically, this research effort provides retail manufacturers to make accurate predictions, optimize resource allocation, and enable real-time decision support.

articleTitle: Towards Energy-Efficient Intelligent Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This research focuses on energy-efficient edge computing in the context of intelligent edge computing. With the increasing demand for computation and data processing at edge network nodes, the study explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, specifically reinforcement learning, to enhance energy management. By conducting a comparative analysis of algorithms, including the Markov Decision Process, Q-learning, Fair heuristic, and Random heuristic, on the basis of waiting time of servers, response time, and energy consumption, the research aims to identify the most effective approach for optimizing the intelligent edge system. Simulations using the iFogSim simulator kit provide empirical evidence for performance evaluation. The findings highlight the advantages of AI-based schemes and emphasize the need for further advancements in intelligent edge computing applications.

articleTitle: The Future of Disassembly Planning: A Critical Assessment of Industry 5.0, Lean, and X-Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Disassembly is a key step in most end-of-life (EoL) product recycling strategies. Traditional disassembly entails paradigmatic and technological shifts to support process planning. Industry 5.0 and X-reality (XR) are notable representatives in this context. With the extension of societal transformation, Industry 5.0 aims to build a human-technology or human-machine companion to emphasize the importance of human safety and well-being. XR encompasses virtual and augmented reality technologies and addresses the human-reality gap in virtual worlds. By leveraging XR to simulate and visualize product information and experimental operations, disassembly planning can be facilitated. However, the roles of Industry 5.0 and XR in EoL disassembly remain underexplored, and the existing literature has neglected the possibility of linking them with lean. This paper first reviewed the extant literature on the potential association of Industry 5.0, lean, and XR for disassembly planning, offering one of the first research articles to highlight current trends. This paper further presented the preliminary work by constructing a tri-dimensional framework to combine three paradigms of human-centric, smart, and lean in the disassembly domain under Industry 5.0. Our findings not only underline the emerging gaps and the unexplored areas but also offer a valuable framework to advance digital disassembly transformation.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Linear and Nonlinear Precoding for Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) answers the exponentially increasing demand for comprehensive fixed broadband and broadcast wireless communication services. Massive MIMO is a pivotal technology in the 5G and beyond (5GaB) wireless communication systems. This paper compares linear precoding algorithms such as Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE), Neumann Series Approximation (NSA) with nonlinear precoders such as Tomlinson-Harashima Precoder (THP), and Lattice Reduction (LR) algorithm, the Lenstra-Lenstra-Lov'asz (LLL) precoder. The comparison was conducted using Bit-Error Rate (BER) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) performance measures. Simulated results prove that nonlinear precoders outperform linear precoding in high SNR regions.

articleTitle: Predicting Survival HIV/AIDS Patients Using Machine Learning Methods: Artificial Neural Network and Decision Tree Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In Burundi, Anti Retroviral Therapy(ART) helps to control infected people living with Immunodeficiency Virus/Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome(HIV/AIDS), but the rate of deaths is still high. This paper presents a model for predicting the survival of HIV/AIDS patients treated in health institution” Association Nationale de Soutien aux Seropositifs et Malades du SIDA” (ANSS) in Burundi. Algorithms of Artificial Neural Network(ANN) and Decision Tree(DT) were used for predicting the survival of People Living With HIV(PLWHIV) under the ANSS health care departments. The results show that the average probability of survival of patients at ANSS institution was 90.2% for an average follow-up period of 5 years. The developed model will help ANSS institution and the Ministry of Health to define effective management strategies for these HIV/AIDS patients.

articleTitle: Recommending Related Research Papers by Topic Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The modern world generates information at an ever-increasing rate. This information explosion also includes the number of published academic research papers. Researchers have access to a variety of digital libraries to retrieve information. Digital libraries often offer access to a number of journal articles and books. Although digital libraries have search mechanisms, it still takes much time to find related research papers. To ease the process of searching for related research papers, The main objective of this study was to develop a model that uses machine learning techniques to recommend related research papers based on an input research paper. The model is implemented and demonstrated using a prototype. The prototype was used to graphically define a model for the creation of a system to recommend related research papers.

articleTitle: Internet Of Things: Sensor Layer Security Risk Mitigation Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The growth of fourth industrial revolution technologies has been driven by the concept of the Internet of Things (IoT), which encompasses devices ranging from personal gadgets to large industrial machines. Through IoT, devices can be connected to the physical world around them, providing a significant increase in connectivity. However, this heightened connectivity has also piqued the interest of attackers who are always on the lookout for vulnerabilities to exploit. Sensor vulnerabilities are one of the most significant threats to IoT devices, primarily due to their limited computing power and the lack of proper security procedures to control sensor usage. Attackers can exploit sensors, such as the camera, accelerometer, moisture sensor, gyroscope, microphone, temperature sensor, light sensor, among others, to extract data or execute malicious code on the IoT device. In this study the various risks and vulnerabilities targeting IoT devices are examined, particularly in relation to sensor misuse, and propose a framework to mitigate sensor-based threats. The effectiveness of the proposed framework was validated through an expert review exercise.

articleTitle: Literature Research on the Use and Requirements of Datagram Communication and Protocols in AAS and Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The emergence of technologies such as the Internet of Things and Industry 4.0 has brought about a digital transformation that is revolutionizing asset management across different industries. Digital Twins are virtual replicas of physical assets that facilitate operational efficiency and data-driven decision-making at the heart of this transformation.. The Asset Administration Shell acts as a Digital Twin for physical and virtual assets, ensuring interoperability and improved management throughout the asset's lifecycle. Communication protocols like Message Queuing Telemetry Transport, Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture, and Constrained Application Protocol are integral to the interpretability goal, enabling reliable data transmission in digital twin systems. This paper delves into the significance of datagrams and communication protocols in Digital Twins, exploring their applications, benefits, and selection criteria for the appropriate protocols. Furthermore, the paper highlights successful implementations of the Asset Administration Shell and provides case studies from various industries. By filling research gaps and providing recommendations, this paper aims to contribute to deploying and understanding digital twins in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Load-Data Imputation and Economic Feasibility Analysis of an Academic Institution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This study focuses on utilizing linear regression for imputing missing data in the context of electrical load profile analysis. Specifically, the study aims to utilize complete time series electric load profile data from the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IITG) campus in Assam, India. The collected data is subjected to a linear regression analysis to impute missing values. The imputed data is then utilized for an economic feasibility analysis of solar photovoltaic (SPV) systems, emphasizing an increased fraction of renewable energy. The imputed data is further utilized for an economic feasibility analysis of solar photovoltaic (SPV) systems with an increased fraction of renewable energy. The analysis, conducted using the HOMER-Pro software, provides valuable insights into the economic viability and sustainability implications of integrating higher fractions of renewable energy in the energy mix of academic institutions. The findings of this study contribute to the development of accurate and comprehensive load profile datasets and highlight the potential benefits of implementing SpV systems with increased renewable energy fraction (REF).

articleTitle: Evaluation of OSS-Enabled OpenRAN Compliant 5G StandAlone Campus Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Open source software (OSS) implementations of 5G campus networks are essential for facilitating researchers to evaluate and validate use cases and applications using customized 5G network configurations. These configurations provide specific performance, such as guaranteed bandwidth, low latency, high reliability, and increased flexibility. To realize a campus network that is both adaptable and cost-effective, it is imperative to overcome the limitations imposed by vendor lock-ins. This objective can be accomplished through the adoption of open network architectures and software-defined networking concepts, which enable the realization of 5G networks using non-proprietary and programmable hardware. Furthermore, the utilization of accessible OSS helps reduce licensing costs while expanding the possibilities for customization. Thus, this research paper presents a modular, cost-efficient, future-proof, and flexible 5G standalone campus network deployed at the Technische Universität Berlin, designed for research and validation of candidate use cases in the drive towards Open Campus Networks. The paper presents a qualitative evaluation of the different OSS RAN implementations, as well as a comparative analysis of performance achieved by different combinations and interworking of radio access and core network software frameworks.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Fractional-Order PID Based on A COVID-19 Optimization Tracking Control for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper seeks to enrich the dynamic performance of Electric Vehicle (EV). The key to achieve this purpose is selecting advanced control strategies. Untraditional COVID-19 optimization technique had been utilized to determine the correct parameters values for the fuzzy FOPID, fuzzy PID, and PID controllers. These controllers are executed on the electric vehicle (EV) to track a preselected speed profile. The foremost objective of the developed controllers is to improve the behavior of the EV such as shrinking the steady-state error, decreasing the rise time, and increasing comfortability. Most of the EV models were high-order systems and have uncertainty parameters. So, this paper uses fuzzy logic control and COVID-19 optimization to overcome these problems. Each control technique is optimized using the COVID-19 algorithm based on several new objective functions. Three cases were considered to investigate the proposed controllers, the first case was applied on a stationary reference speed while the second case was executed at vehicle acceleration and the last case was implemented when the vehicle deceleration. The presented results display that the fuzzy FOPID controller adjusted by the COVID-19 optimization can absorb the EV uncertainty and nonlinearity. It achieved a minimum rise-time and the least steady-state-error compared to the other control techniques. Moreover, it has no overshoot in the speed which guarantees comfort for the EV.

articleTitle: Development of Program Application Based on Mie Theory for Calculating the Optical Extinction of Au and Ag Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In the las two decades noble metals nanoparticles (NPs) have been widely studied in materials science and nan-otechnology. This has been motivated because such noble metals NPs have unique characteristics and properties that make them important in various applications in nanotechnology. Particu-larly, the characteristic of localized surface plas monic resonance (LSPR) has been exploited for various nano applications. The plasmonic resonance strongly depends on the geometry of the NPs, the type of metal, the size of the NPs and the scattering of electromagnetic radiation that occurs when light and matter of NPs interact. Generally, in a first approximation the spherical NPs are studied as an ideal case, also experimentally is easy to synthesize those noble metals NPS. Theoretically, the dispersion of electromagnetic radiation from a sphere is defined by the Mie Theory. This requires calculations that can become lengthy and even impossible for those with limited resources. Therefore, in this work a program was developed in Python to obtain the extinction coefficients for Au and Ag nanoparticles. The algorithms used were implemented in a cluster of new generation pocket called Parallella. The use of this computational methodology allows the study and obtaining of the extinction coefficients of Ag and Au NPs successfully, this being easily adaptable methodology for other metals where can calculate and/or simulate a variety of optical properties.

articleTitle: Model for Recognition of Personal Protective Equipment in Construction Applying YOLO-v5 and YOLO-v7
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Due to the nature of activities carried out during a construction, companies find it necessary to stablish controls to avoid accidents caused by the lack of personal safety equipment. However, this process often involves manual supervision carried out by a specific staff. Due to this, there is no efficient control, nor constant monitoring to prevent this type of accident. For this reason, a model is proposed that recognizes the use of personal protective equipment in construction through 2 deep learning models: YOLO-v5 and YOLO-v7. Four stages were carried out: (i) data collection, (ii) data processing, (iii) training and (iv) evaluation of results. A dataset of 743 images composed of 6 classes was used: boots, glasses, gloves, helmet, person, and safety vest. The results show that the Yolo v7 model obtains a 0.873, while Yolo v5 obtains a 0.796. These values represent the combination of precision and recall in mAP@0.5, therefore v7 was more optimal than Yolo v5. Additionally, the study shows which is the recognition pattern for both algorithms, this pattern helps us to reinforce the detection of objects through training.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review of Probabilistic Model-Based Approaches for Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Heart disease is a global health concern, contributing considerably to global death rates. Predicting heart disease accurately and on time is critical to improve healthcare outcomes. Recent technological breakthroughs have resulted in the creation of prediction models, which are increasingly being used in proactive healthcare efforts. Probabilistic techniques have gained relevance among these models due to their capacity to handle ambiguity in medical data. This paper undertakes a systematic literature review to evaluate the use of probabilistic model-based techniques in the prediction of heart disease. This paper presents the common research themes in heart disease prediction and probabilistic models, highlighting areas that need more attention. In addition, the paper discusses the effectiveness of probabilistic models in the context of heart disease prediction, drawing attention to their unique capacity to quantify prediction uncertainty. Overall, this paper highlights the promise that these probabilistic models have for improving diagnostic precision and efficacy in clinical settings dedicated to heart disease care.
